summary.intent: Fix two #242 review findings on PR #634: (1) E2BIG from files_containing_at putting every baseline key in git grep argv, by sending patterns via run_with_stdin with 'git grep -f -' and migrating test runners; (2) make the resumption positive control work under both native and single-level tag listing shapes. Then run the full gate, a targeted Codex review, and make a signed commit without pushing.
summary.outcome: Both fixes were implemented with failing reproductions first; the small and 8,831-key CLI cases now both plan cargo/foo 1.0.0 -> 1.0.1-alpha.0, and the legacy-listing tests pass natively and under the one-level shim. The full gate (pre-push, lint, doc-check, test, fuzz-check, bench) passed by exit code and a signed commit was created. The targeted Codex review and the report with the sha had not yet happened in the transcript.

repo: files_containing_at in callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs now sends patterns through run_with_stdin with 'git grep -f -'; newline-in-needle splitting matches -e semantics, and error text no longer includes the needle list.

Test runners (FakeRunner, CountingGrep, ScriptedGit, LegacyTagListing, RealGitRunner and the scripted tag fakes) must delegate run_with_stdin or grep silently falls back to the conservative path, so they need migrating whenever the transport changes.
Temporarily making the default run_with_stdin panic on grep was an effective audit to find unmigrated runners (15 graph lib tests plus 1 integration test).
git grep -f - cost scales with pattern count (about 3.8s for 8,831 keys), which is Git's own per-pattern cost; the large test payload was shrunk to about 2.5 MB to keep it fast.
The worktree guard requires scripts to be run from files rather than inline commands.
Bench process counts stay constant across 50/200/500 packages after the change.

code.finding: files_containing_at and RealGit gained stdin-based grep transport; new tests cover argv form and a real E2BIG-sized payload.
CountingGrep now delegates stdin and counts grep calls there.
The resumption positive control now covers both native recursive peeling and single-level listing shapes, so it passes under the one-level shim.

workflow: Reproduce each finding with the supplied script before changing code, then rerun it after the fix to confirm.
Run mktemp-based probes in $TMPDIR with fail-closed checks; a failed mktemp ran a probe in the worktree and left stray files that had to be unstaged and removed.
Run the gate in the background with a monitor on per-step exit codes.
